summary: Another test - but the lock-down you ran in terminal 1 was applied to /home/docker_user/catkin_ws/src/contact_maintain/scripts/test/, not the active workspace at /home/docker_user/catkin_ws/src/contact_maintain/test/. Verification: test/.cursor/rules/after_each_chat.mdc is still -rw-r--r-- with no .cursorignore in that folder, while scripts/test/.cursor/rules/after_each_chat.mdc is -r--r--r-- and has .cursorignore. To actually protect the live rule, run from the correct folder: cd /home/docker_user/catkin_ws/src/contact_maintain/test && chmod 444 .cursor/rules/after_each_chat.mdc && echo '.cursor/rules/after_each_chat.mdc' > .cursorignore. Caveat: .cursorignore only stops Cursor from reading/sending the file to the model and editing it via the agent; chmod stops POSIX writes (the agent's write tool will fail). Combined, the extension cannot rewrite it. I did NOT modify the rule file this turn - only the tmp summary file was written.
